To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) child poverty is associated with worse outcomes in terms of health, education, behaviour and social outcomes for UK children and (2) there are gaps in the evidence with regard to child health outcomes and the impact of policies and interventions to address child poverty.
child poverty is a major problem for children in the UK, with serious and long-lasting health consequences, and that child health professionals should be actively working to reduce it.

child poverty is a major public health problem in the UK; it is linked to a wide range of poor health outcomes in children; there is a strong evidence base to support action to reduce child poverty and its consequences; and child health professionals can play a role in supporting and promoting action on child poverty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the impact of child poverty on health and well-being.
the impact of poverty on child health, but we are also concerned with the health impact of child health.
the health consequences of poverty, and with how child health professionals and services can contribute to the reduction of child poverty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
child poverty is bad for child health, and that the evidence for this is compelling.
child poverty is bad for the health and well-being of children, and that child health professionals can play a key role in tackling this problem.
poverty has a negative impact on child health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
poverty is bad for children's health, and that the best way for health professionals to improve child health is to support policies to reduce poverty.
child poverty is a key social determinant of child health, and that child health professionals have a role to play in reducing the negative health impacts of child poverty.

the health and well-being of children is strongly associated with the economic circumstances in which they are brought up, and that the health of children in poverty in the UK is worse than the health of children not in poverty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
child poverty is associated with poor health outcomes and poor educational outcomes for children, with negative consequences for society.
the health of children in the UK is being damaged by child poverty, and that this can be prevented.

child health professionals should be aware of the links between child health and poverty and should take action at a local level, in the UK and beyond, to reduce child poverty and its health consequences.
